title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) that tests whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success beyond a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration task bank and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design details, execution accounting, representative artifact-grounded validator traces, quantitative analysis, diagnostic interpretation of the degenerate outcome, and artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered arms (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction: Motivation and research question. The promise of LLMs and agentic orchestrators for network operations (NetOps) hinges on safe, verifiable acceptance criteria for generated actions and configurations. Practical deployments therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and optional repair steps in generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines to reduce silent or wrong-but-plausible actions. Despite this architectural convergence, systematic, preregistered, artifact-grounded measurements of validator coverage (false-positive and false-negative rates), detection latency, and the marginal contribution of repair to end-to-end guarded success in NetOps remain limited. We designed study AC-2026-03 to measure the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Research question: Can a standardized, empirically estimable validator metric suite (coverage, FP-rate, FN-rate, mean detection latency, operational-impact proxy) predict end-to-end guarded success better than a single raw verifier pass rate in a controlled GVR NetOps benchmark? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired confirmation run (n=200 pairs) executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics with explicit accountings of model calls, provider audit, and validator traces. (2) Exact, artifact-grounded reporting of a degenerate but reproducible outcome (complete ceiling) with diagnostic interpretation that identifies design intersections (single-sample generation, deterministic validator, synthetic tasks) that produced the ceiling. (3) Concrete, artifact-supported, preregisterable follow-up arms (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to produce estimable validator FP/FN and repair utility.
sections.related_work: Positioning and synthesis. Prior work documents the emergence of GVR-like architectures and verifier-guided flows in code and system domains and their proposed value to reduce stochastic generator errors and provide deterministic acceptance criteria [1]. Recent NetOps- and AIOps-focused benchmark efforts emphasize operational failure modes—ticket noise, false premises, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that motivate insertion of verifier layers but do not provide a standardized validator-metric suite adapted to NetOps GVR flows [2],[3]. Prototype system reports propose self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair to reduce action-triggering failures in tool-augmented LLM systems [4]. Surveys of LLMs for telecommunications and NetOps discuss adaptation and verifier trade-offs and argue for measurement of verification cost versus nominal correctness [5]. From these records we extract two bounded conclusions: (i) GVR-style designs are advocated and demonstrated in prototypes and adjacent domains; (ii) the empirical coverage of mechanistic validators across heterogeneous NetOps scenarios remains an open measurement gap. Our study targets that measurement gap under strict preregistration and artifact archival; we avoid extrapolating beyond the experimental scope supported by the cited record set.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and high-level design. The study was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Key preregistered parameters (execution manifest / preregistration fields): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini; task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test: exact two-sided McNemar test with paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Power plan targeted detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 with α=0.05 and ~80% power for n=200 pairs; bootstrap stability checks were preregistered.

Task generation, constraints, and contamination controls. Tasks were deterministically sampled from a synthetic generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) in the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family. Each task encodes: initial_state, expected_final_state, a compact natural-language intent, allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups), and a required_command_sequence. Difficulty labels included 'very_hard' and 'extreme' per the preregistered challenging_workflow_stress_v1 index. Contamination/exclusion rules (preregistered) included duplicate-output SHA-256 exclusion and semantic-similarity exclusion (embedding cosine > 0.95) with deterministic replacement. The archive (analysis/contamination_summary.csv) shows no exclusions in this run.

Model and sampling configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Execution accounting (execution manifest): model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair); maximum_model_calls = 400 as preregistered; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0. Important recorded configuration: execution/model_configuration.json lists temperature = null (temperature = null/unset). We explicitly report that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic provider-side sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; it is a recorded configuration field and provider-side sampling variability may still exist. The adapter provider-call audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with exactly one shared initial generation per task.

Validator, scoring rule, and permitted repair. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator implements mechanistic intent-constraint checks and emits per-episode fields: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and remediation artifacts when repairs are used. The preregistered binary scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) uses validator.valid as the success label. The pipeline allowed at most one repair call when validator.valid == false; repair traces and repair_applied flags are recorded. Preregistered exclusion rules mark repairs that introduce actions outside allowed action sets as policy-violating and count such repairs as failures for the primary outcome.

Analysis plan and reproducibility provisions. Primary analysis used the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided with bootstrap percentile CIs (10,000 resamples). Missingness and retry rules: maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries); primary analysis uses complete pairs only; sensitivity analyses were preregistered to treat missing/incomplete episodes in guarded as failures. All raw outputs, provider-call traces, validator traces, task manifests, and analysis artifacts (including analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) are archived and referenced in the execution bundle to permit independent reproducibility and reanalysis.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (shared-initial generation per pair). Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. No preregistered contamination exclusions occurred (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Confirmatory statistics. Per analysis/condition_summary.csv, baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. These numeric values are archived in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and match the preregistered analysis executor outputs.

Representative artifact-grounded validator-trace excerpt. We reproduce verbatim key fields from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json to illustrate validator outputs (values copied from the archived artifact):
  - pair_id: pair-000004
  - normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
  - parsed_command_count: 4
  - required_command_count: 4
  - observed_touched_field_count: 3
  - valid: true
  - repair_applied: false
  - validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
  - validator_version: 5.0
For this exemplar the parsed and required command counts match, no violation codes were emitted, and the validator did not request repair. Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode; repair_applied = false for all 400 episodes (no repairs invoked).

Exploratory diagnostics. Because every sampled shared initial candidate passed the validator, per-validator false-positive and false-negative empirical estimates are degenerate (no observed FP or FN). Detection-latency and repair-invocation distributions are uninformative. The execution bundle nevertheless contains full per-episode validator traces and raw responses (execution/raw_results.jsonl) enabling reanalysis under alternative scoring definitions or under injected faults.
sections.discussion:
Why the ceiling occurred (diagnostic interpretation). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline and guarded conditions evaluated the identical initial candidate per pair; therefore any paired difference could originate only from deterministic validator-triggered repair. The degenerate all-valid outcome is artifact-grounded and arises from three documented, interlocking determinants visible in the archive: (1) the synthetic generator produced candidates that satisfied the validator's mechanistic constraints for the sampled seeds and the task-encoding used by the generator; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling regime (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1) eliminated generator variability as a source of disagreement; and (3) the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but cannot detect some classes of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent) without an external intent model or operator feedback. These points are supported by the archived task manifests, responses, and validator traces.

Implications for measurement and operational evaluation. The paired, shared_initial_candidate design is a strict and useful isolator: it ensures that any observed paired improvement must be produced downstream by validator-triggered repair rather than by generator sampling. However, this same design elevates the risk of degenerate single-sample ceilings when the generator and validator align on the sampled draws. For measurement of validator coverage and repair utility the design trade-offs are therefore explicit: (a) shared_initial_candidate isolates repair but requires non-trivial baseline failure prevalence to observe repair benefits; (b) multi-sample or fault-injection arms increase baseline failure prevalence and generator variability and hence enable estimation of FP/FN and repair value; (c) multi-validator comparisons and multi-model execution improve external validity across validator designs and generator behaviors.

Artifact-grounded, preregistered follow-up prescriptions. Each proposal below is implementable within the archived adapter semantics and is explicitly supported by the execution bundle's deterministic task-replacement and contamination controls: (1) Fault-injection arm (preregistered): deterministically inject a controlled set of faults into reference answers for a specified fraction f of tasks (syntactic omissions, configuration-logic faults, semantic-intent swaps). This produces measurable baseline invalidity and creates opportunities to quantify repair effectiveness. (2) Multi-sample stochastic generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task (independent seeds recorded). Let the guarded pipeline accept any validator-approved candidate among the k draws or attempt repair on rejected draws. This reveals generator variability and allows valuation of validator screening power. (3) Multi-validator and multi-model comparison: add at least one alternative validator implementation and at least one additional model family to quantify sensitivity to validator design and model idiosyncrasies. Implementing these arms will produce non-degenerate data suitable for estimating FP/FN, detection latency, repair utility, and predictive R^2 against operational-impact proxies as originally planned.

Threats to validity and limitations (artifact-grounded). Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate choice was preregistered and intentionally isolates downstream repair but concentrates single-sample ceiling risk. Construct validity: validator.valid operationalizes mechanistic correctness but may not capture semantic intent misalignment. External validity: synthetic task bank, the single-model execution (gpt-5-mini), and the single deterministic validator limit generalization to heterogeneous production networks and alternative model families. Conclusion validity: the degenerate outcome produced zero variance in the primary estimand; hence inferential conclusions about validator benefit are not supported by this execution alone. All these threats and limitations are recorded in the archived manifests and analysis artifacts and motivate the concrete follow-up arms above.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to evaluate validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank and sampled gpt-5-mini generations used here, every sampled initial candidate passed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and no repairs were applied; guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). This ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally targeted 10-percentage-point improvement. The outcome is artifact-grounded and reproducible from the archived bundle. We publish exact execution and analysis artifacts and provide concrete, preregistered follow-up arms—fault injection, multi-sample generation, and multi-validator comparison—that are required to produce estimable validator FP/FN behavior and to quantify repair value in operationally meaningful conditions.

Sampling/generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled generation per task reused for baseline and guarded); execution/model_configuration.json recorded temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). All raw outputs, per-episode validator traces, execution manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json). No human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
